newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian 1997 budget seen largely effective.
newsitem.headline: Italian 1997 budget seen largely effective.

text.p: Italy's 1997 budget looks largely on course to meet its tough deficit-cutting targets, with only a few of the measures failing to live up to expectations, Italian newsagency Agi quoted the Treasury as saying.

Agi said a report from a Treasury working group that is monitoring public finances estimated that the corrective measures included in the budget might bring around two trillion lire less than expected. But it added that this shortfall would be made up elsewhere.

"At the current moment, the targets laid down by the budget seem to be largely respected," Agi quoted the report as saying. "However in some sectors, problems persist over obtaining the forecast savings," the report added, warning ministries to maintain close vigilance on their spending.
No-one was immediately available at the Treasury to comment on the report.

Agi said the working group had pin-pointed problems at the education ministry, which was struggling to deal with a growing number of students, and the employment ministry, which has so far failed to persuade many public workers to leave full-time posts for part-time positions.

In addition, the transport ministry still had to find reductions in management costs for local transport networks and the health ministry had been slow to activate budget measures due to raise 690 billion lire.
The defence, post and finance ministries also had more work to do before they reached their 1997 targets.

Italy has pledged to cut its deficit to three percent of gross domestic product (GDP) this year, as demanded by the Maastricht Treaty for countries wishing to join the single European currency, from 6.7 percent in 1996.
To achieve that goal, the 1997 budget contained some 62.5 trillion lire of deficit cuts.
